touches.text: Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.
The launcher is Python (bin/cairn), run by Cairn's own interpreter, so Windows needs no bash. Typing `cairn` works on either platform.

Scripts are Python wherever possible, run by Cairn's own interpreter, so one file works on every platform. Platform-specific ones match their platform: executable or .sh on Linux; .bat, .cmd or .ps1 on Windows.
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.

What the waker starts outlives whoever started it (detached, or through systemd-run --user, which gives it its own memory cap and log while still deciding nothing). Restarting a shim never takes down the bus it once woke.

The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien until the outline is implemented; a design agent comes after that. Until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.
Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).
Test tiers: commit, hourly, daily and weekly. Each tier runs only what it must, so a commit needs only its own proofs and the long runs wait for the long tiers; nothing runs just in case.

A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal.

conflicts.ticket_says: bin/cairn must be run as `bash bin/cairn` on Windows; it is a bash script that cannot be executed bare on Windows
conflicts.why: The outline states: 'The launcher is Python (bin/cairn), run by Cairn's own interpreter, so Windows needs no bash.' The ticket demonstrates bin/cairn is currently bash, contradicting the outline's claim that it is Python and that Windows needs no bash to run it. One says the launcher IS Python; the other shows it IS bash.
